text:
Maya: Quick sync — preparing Azalea-7B for the model-catalog prelaunch. Need green checks on: licensing, perf profiles for 512/2048 contexts, a small set of sample queries for the eval harness, and embedding tensor shape compatibility for the embeddings endpoint. @Ada, can you confirm curation artifacts?
Ada: On it. Curation manifest uploaded to GDrive and I left a note in the sheet about data provenance. Licenses: Apache-2 for base weights but there’s a third-party tokenizer clip with a CLA — tagging @Devon.
Devon: Saw the CLA. We need the signed form from the tokenizer repo to ship publicly. I emailed the maintainer; ETA 48h if they respond. If not, we either vendor a different tokenizer or ship behind an access flag.
Maya: Ok — vendor fallback plan makes sense. Ryan — runtime perf? last smoke run looked close but we saw memory spike at 2k context on the 80GB A100 nodes.
Ryan: Spike is reproducible with dense batch of 16 and 2k context. My notes: GC churn due to kv-cache allocation pattern. I pushed a patch to reduce peak KV allocation (PR #4123). Need a quick canary run.
Sam: I can run the canary with the patched runtime. Will also test dynamic batching at 1/2/4/8 to measure p95 latency impact. Sam: planning runs in staging at 11:30 PST, will post results here.
Priya: For embeddings: Azalea's embedding head returns 1x1536 floats. The catalog embeddings API expects (batch, dim). Confirming batch behavior: model returns single vector per request; we handle batch aggregation client-side. Any shape mismatch?
Ada: The curation pipeline currently yields lists of texts; our ingest converts to batch embeddings by calling the embeddings endpoint per-item (not batching). That explains higher cost. We should change to batch calls.
Maya: Good catch. Can we change ingest to batch size 64? What about edge cases for short docs?
Sam: Batch 64 is fine memory-wise on dedicated pools but try 32 for staging first. Also check tokenization overhead.
Maya: Also need a tiny sample query set (10-12 prompts) representing search, summarization, and QA to run through the catalog eval harness. I sketched three — can people add 1-2 each? Put them in the shared doc: https://go/redwood/azalea-prelaunch (private)
Ada: Added 4 sample QA prompts and 2 summarization ones. Example QA snippet I added:```
Q: "Summarize the key risk factors for using a finite-state scheduler in production."
Expected: short bulleted list, mention fairness and starvation.
```
Ryan: Ran the staging canary (with PR #4123) — quick numbers: 512 ctx, batch16 p95 120ms; 2048 ctx, batch8 p95 420ms with reduced OOMs (was failing before). Logs: `kv_alloc_peak=11.4GB`. Baseline without patch had ~18GB.
Priya: Embedding throughput test (batch32) gave 350 req/s on the dedicated pool; per-embedding cost projection looks good. Changed ingest to batch32 in a branch: `feature/batch-embeds`.
Devon: Legal update: if maintainer doesn't reply by EOD tomorrow, we can't publish the tokenizer. Alternative is to ship Azalea with a documented replacement tokenizer under MIT we already vetted. Need decision by noon tomorrow.
Maya: Decision path noted. Ada/Devon coordinate. If we vendor MIT tokenizer, update curation manifest and call it out in release notes.
Sam: Canary full results posted here: https://go/redwood/canary-1718902468 — latency graphs, p95/p99, memory traces. I flagged a repeatable regression in sampling path when temperature >1.0 (small tail latency bump).
Ryan: Acknowledged. I'll instrument the sampling kernels to check attention kernel selection under high temperature.
Ada: One more: eval harness found a subtle tokenization discrepancy on code-like inputs — extra whitespace tokens causing scoring diffs. I attached a minimal repro in the doc.
Priya: I can normalize whitespace in ingest as a stopgap. Will PR normalization change later today.
Maya: Action items summary: 1) Devon & Ada — finalize tokenizer license fallback by noon tomorrow. 2) Sam — run another canary with batch32 embeddings + temp stress test. 3) Ryan — add sampling instrumentation & follow KV allocation reduction. 4) Priya — open PR for batching ingest (branch `feature/batch-embeds`) and whitespace normalization. 5) Ada — update curation manifest if we swap tokenizer.
Devon: I'll draft the fallback text for release notes and post here when done.
deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: azalea-7b-staging -> 2024-12-01T19:30:00Z (initiated by Sam).
Maya: Thanks everyone. If we hit all green checks (license or fallback in place, canary perf within targets, embedding batching enabled), we can target catalog publish for next Thursday. Please ping any blockers asap. :eyes:
